messages:
lina_support: we have ~12 customers reporting 503s starting ~15:06 UTC, most from embed-heavy endpoints. CS page getting noisy :rotating_light:

maria: saw the alerts too — upstream worker restart spike in hosted-pool-42, lots of OOM+segfaults in the same window

kenji: pasting a trimmed log from one container: ```
[2026-06-02T15:05:48Z] infer-runner[pid:2312]: kv_prefetch: alloc 1.2G -> CUDA error: out of memory
[2026-06-02T15:05:49Z] infer-runner[pid:2312]: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7ffd...
[2026-06-02T15:05:49Z] system: container restart (exit_code=139)
```

sara_oncall: paging metrics: hosted-pool-42 worker_restarts p95 jumped from 0 → 18/sec, p50 latency for embed API spiked to 2.4s then 30s before 503s flood

jack_engineer: confirmed correlated with large-embed batch QPS bump from a single customer job — they sent 3 concurrent large-context embed requests with batch_size=96 around the same time (uncommon pattern)

lina_support: customers reporting timeouts then 503s, some on paid plans. CS opened tickets and asked for ETA. Is there a temporary mitigation?

maria: immediate: 1) route affected customers to fallback pool 2) scale up hosted-pool-42 by 2 nodes (hot) 3) throttling/circuit-break on embed endpoint for batch_size > 64  — doing step 1 now

deploy-bot: reroute request: route-policy apply --pool hosted-pool-42 --fallback hosted-pool-99 --selector embed-endpoint — success (ops ticket #INC-6321)

kenji: digging into heap traces — looks like kv-prefetch alloc path does not account for combined batched sequence memory when batch_size>64 + large dims. Repro locally with our stress harness: ```bash
# repro harness
python tools/embed_burst.py --concurrency 3 --batch 96 --seq-len 8192 --model redwood/open-embed-xxl
```

jack_engineer: i can repro in staging within 3 runs, we hit a cudaMemcpy failing then SIGSEGV inside attention kernel. Suspect a regression introduced with the last prefetch change (commit c3f9e8) that preallocs KV buffers optimistically

sara_oncall: mitigation status: fallback routing done, autoscaler triggered +2 nodes, throttling rule applied. Error rate down ~85% in last 3m but p95 latency still elevated for rerouted requests

lina_support: CS updated customers: temporary mitigation in place, engineering investigating root cause, will update in 30 min. They asked about billing credits for impacted calls — finance flagged for review

kenji: initial root-cause hypothesis: kv-prefetch prealloc doesn't clamp by available GPU memory across combined batched requests, causing oversubscription during concurrent large embed bursts -> OOM -> segfault. Patch idea: add global prefetch budget and a safe-fail to fall back to on-demand prefetch when budget exceeded

jack_engineer: putting up a short-lived hotfix on staging: small change to prefetch allocator to cap at 60% of device free mem and fall back. ready to test, rolling to canary now

deploy-bot: deploy start: infra/canary/kv-prefetch-cap-2026-06-02-1 -> canary hosts (2)

maria: canary logs look good so far — no OOMs on the canary under the harness. Can we push to pooled hosts and monitor?

jack_engineer: plan: 1) roll change to one AZ of hosted-pool-42 (30% traffic) 2) monitor worker_restarts, OOMs, p99 latency 3) if green, full roll. rolling now

sara_oncall: noted. paging hooks updated for regression. alert thresholds temporarily relaxed to avoid noise. cs asked for a short summary to include in customer update

lina_support: copy for CS (please edit): "We observed a surge of large concurrent embed requests that caused upstream GPU memory oversubscription in hosted inference. We routed traffic to a fallback pool and applied throttling; engineering deployed a hotfix that caps prefetch allocation under high concurrency. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem and any billing remediation."

maria: LGTM — add timeline and who to contact for urgent follow-ups (oncall + support)

kenji: post-deploy check (10m): canary→no OOMs, pooled roll 30%→no increased restarts, error rate down to baseline. setting postmortem owner = jack_engineer + kenji. require repro case, root cause, and long-term fix (allocator rewrite + unit tests)

jack_engineer: archived reproducer in infra-tests: tests/kv_prefetch/large_burst_repro.py and added a regression job to run nightly on staging. I'll start the postmortem doc after we stabilize

sara_oncall: CS: we can tell customers fix deployed and we are monitoring, offer to follow up with billing contacts if needed. ops: keep an eye on hosted-pool-42 for 24h

lina_support: thanks everyone. final ask: if anyone sees any late restarts tag me @lina_support immediately. closing initial incident channel thread, will continue updates in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
